terms.comment: + dative of the person; prō + ablative of the thing. grātiās agere is thanking in words; grātiam referre is repaying in deed (Cic. Off. I 47).

phrases.latin: Pater caelestis, ā quō omne dōnum perfectum dēscendit, grātiās tibi agimus prō hōc cibō … et prō hāc domō
phrases.english: Heavenly Father, from whom every perfect gift comes down, we thank you for this food … and for this home

phrases.latin: Cōnfitēminī Dominō, quoniam bonus: quoniam in aeternum misericordia ejus.
phrases.english: Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good: for his mercy endures for ever (said responsively, Dad the first half-verse and Theo the second).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 393, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
